summary: Network subsystem teardown. Drains and releases two mutexes (handles at this+0xAD8 and this+0xAF4, each waited on with its own timeout at +0xADC and +0xAF8), then destroys the mutex-protected linked lists, runs the subsystem cleanup helper sub_57E570, and invokes the virtual cleanup method at vtable+48. Finally, if the Winsock-initialized flag at this+0xA74 is set, calls WSACleanup, clears the flag to 0 and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.

operations.description: If the first mutex handle at this+0xAD8 is non-null, wait on it with the timeout stored at this+0xADC via WaitForSingleObject.
If the first mutex handle at this+0xAD8 is non-null, release it with ReleaseMutex.
If the second mutex handle at this+0xAF4 is non-null, wait on it with the timeout stored at this+0xAF8 via WaitForSingleObject.
If the second mutex handle at this+0xAF4 is non-null, release it with ReleaseMutex.
Run the subsystem-specific cleanup helper sub_57E570 on this object.
Destroy the thread-safe linked list via ThreadSafeLinkedListDestructionWithMutex.
Invoke the virtual cleanup method at vtable+48, dispatched through the vtable pointer read from this+0x0.
Flush and destroy the first mutex-protected linked list via MutexProtectedLinkedListFlushDestroy.
Destroy the second mutex-protected linked list via MutexProtectedLinkedListDestruction.
If the Winsock-initialized flag at this+0xA74 is zero, return 0 without touching Winsock.
Call WSACleanup to shut down Winsock.
Clear the Winsock-initialized flag at this+0xA74 to 0 after WSACleanup.
Return 1 when WSACleanup was performed, 0 otherwise.
